subtopic: Nucleophilic Substitution Reactions of Alkyl Halides
stem: How will you obtain 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane from alkene? Write possible structures of alkene and the reaction involved.
solution:
Two different alkenes give 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane on addition of \(\mathrm{HBr}\), because in each case Markownikov addition places \(\mathrm{Br}\) on the more substituted carbon, which is the ring carbon already carrying the methyl group.

**(i) 1-Methylcyclohexene** (the double bond is inside the ring, between the methyl-bearing carbon and the next ring carbon):

1-methylcyclohexene \(+\ \mathrm{HBr}\ \longrightarrow\) 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane

The methyl-bearing ring carbon has no hydrogen on it, so by Markownikov's rule \(\mathrm{H}\) adds to the other doubly bonded carbon and \(\mathrm{Br}\) adds to the methyl-bearing carbon, giving the tertiary bromide.

**(ii) Methylenecyclohexane** (the double bond is exocyclic, between the ring carbon and a \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) group):

methylenecyclohexane \(+\ \mathrm{HBr}\ \longrightarrow\) 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane

Here \(\mathrm{H}\) adds to the exocyclic \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) (turning it into the \(\mathrm{CH_3}\) group) and \(\mathrm{Br}\) adds to the ring carbon, which again gives the tertiary bromide.

stem: Arrange the following compounds in order of increasing boiling points : bromoform, chloromethane, dibromomethane, bromomethane.
solution:
The comparative boiling points of halogen derivatives are mainly related with van der Waals forces of attraction which depend upon the molecular size. In the present case all the compounds contain only one carbon. Thus the molecular size depends upon the size of halogen and number of halogen atoms present.

Thus increasing order of boiling point is,

\(\mathrm{CH_3Cl} < \mathrm{CH_3Br} < \mathrm{CH_2Br_2} < \mathrm{CHBr_3}\)

subtopic: Nucleophilic Substitution Reactions of Alkyl Halides
stem: Primary allylic and primary benzylic halides show higher reactivity by \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) mechanism than other primary alkyl halides. Explain.
solution: \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) reaction involves formation of carbocation intermediate. The allylic and benzylic carbocation intermediate formed are resonance stabilized, and hence \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) mechanism is favoured.

subtopic: Nucleophilic Substitution Reactions of Alkyl Halides
stem:
Which of the following two compounds would react faster by \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) mechanism and Why ?

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2Cl}\) (1-Chlorobutane)  and  \(\mathrm{CH_3-CHCl-CH_2-CH_3}\) (2-Chlorobutane)
solution:
In \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) mechanism, a pentacoordinate T.S. is involved. The order of reactivity of alkyl halides towards \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) mechanism is,

Primary \(>\) Secondary \(>\) Tertiary, (due to increasing crowding in T.S. from primary to tertiary halides. 1-Chlorobutane being primary halide will react faster by \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) mechanism, than the secondary halide 2-chlorobutane.
